answer: Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the tundra of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The shale holds work receipts rather than names, so the yarrow of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, slashed on a failed audit, rewards vest against future work.
